headline: A fresh-context critic audited the whole game against its two hard rules — is it fun without the lesson, and does it require understanding rather than answering. Two of three quests passed both; the boss passed all three phases. The Memory Threads board failed for grading the player per card, and 236 authored lines of the conformity act turned out to be unwired. Every finding is back with its builder.

findings.text: THESIS RISK: the Memory Threads board grades each card the moment it lands, prints a running score, and volunteers the answer when wrong — the only screen in the game that looks like a worksheet. Fix: delay anchoring until the player commits a complete board; replace verdicts with statements of physical fact.

All 236 authored lines of quest3_lantern.ts are unwired, including the third naming moment. The shipped inline version reads a textbook definition aloud before the Insight Card repeats it — structurally the same as plan.md's own example of bad dialogue.

The shipped trial answers contradict the ambient dialogue: half the valley says 'I heard third, I said second', but the trial's round three is a different pair. After the emotional peak the villagers describe a trial the player did not play.
TALK.ending and TALK.boss are authored and unwired — the game's final scene does not play.
Room Three as specified is brute-forceable in two attempts (two sequences shown, free retries). The sequence must be constructed from context, not chosen between two demonstrations.

The journal rendered only definition, illustration and terms — misconception, real-world examples and every example the player earned were written and never displayed, tilting the notebook toward a vocabulary list. Now two pages: what happened to you first, formal terms second.

Cut a naming-moment line that told the player they had learned, a Sera idle line that gave away the whole first puzzle before the player had tried it, and an insight-card eyebrow that asserted the player's inner state.
Passes, but both restraint hazards are opt-in — a player who never swings the sword faces only the tower timing. Needs an environmental startle to anticipate, not merely one to abstain from causing.

A session token limit terminated nine in-flight agents mid-edit. Four partial edits were repaired (Web Audio typed-array generics, a half-written event helper, an unexported map symbol); all agents resumed from their transcripts rather than restarting.
Phaser getFrame() returns the __BASE frame for unknown names, so every missing-art guard was drawing the entire 2048px atlas across the scene.
Tile families were keyed by leaf name, so tile/woods/grass_* merged with tile/town/grass_* and the town field rendered as a two-tone checkerboard.
edgePixels treated a tile's own border as a material edge, putting a lit line on the top row of every interior tile — a horizontal band across every path and every water surface in the game.
Grass variants were tone-mismatched and non-periodic, producing per-tile seams and brightness checkerboarding. Now seamless and rank-quantised.

comparisons.title: Town Square vs Stardew Valley world density
comparisons.verdict: Blind A/B: the reference wins all ten criteria. Building facades and the dynamic light layer are ours to keep; the ground layer, prop shadows and the absence of trees are what lose it.

comparisons.title: Festival Plaza vs Stardew Night Market
comparisons.verdict: The event transformation reads: string lights, bunting, a lit ceremonial carpet, stalls and a gathered crowd. Trial lanterns still need mounts.
